questions.q: Two threads call `put` on the same plain `HashMap` at the same time. What is the risk?
o: Lost updates or a corrupted internal structure
The second thread always throws an exception
The map becomes read-only
The map sorts its entries automatically
questions.w: `HashMap` is not thread-safe. Use `ConcurrentHashMap`, or confine the map to one thread.

questions.q: Which statement about `ConcurrentHashMap` in Java 8+ is correct?
o: Writers lock only the affected bin, and reads do not lock at all
A single lock protects the whole map
Reads and writes both take the same global lock
It copies the whole table on every write
questions.w: Empty bins are filled with CAS and occupied bins are locked individually. This lets many threads work in parallel.

questions.q: Which code is a check-then-act race on a `ConcurrentHashMap`?
o: `if (!map.containsKey(k)) map.put(k, v);`
`map.putIfAbsent(k, v);`
`map.computeIfAbsent(k, f);`
`map.merge(k, 1, Integer::sum);`
questions.w: Each call is atomic, but two calls in a row are not. Use the single atomic methods instead.

o: So that `get` returning `null` always means the key is absent
Because null values would be slower to store
Because Java 8 removed null from collections
To save memory in each bin
questions.w: In a concurrent map you cannot safely call `containsKey` afterwards to tell "absent" from "mapped to null", because another thread may change it in between.

questions.q: A list of event listeners is read thousands of times per second and changed once a day. Which collection suits it?
o: `CopyOnWriteArrayList`
`Vector`
`LinkedList` with a lock
`PriorityBlockingQueue`
questions.w: Reads take no lock and iterate a snapshot. Writes copy the whole array, which is fine when they are rare.

questions.q: A producer is faster than its consumers. How does a bounded `BlockingQueue` help?
o: `put` blocks when the queue is full, so the producer slows down
The queue drops the oldest items silently
The queue grows until memory is full
The queue converts itself into a topic
questions.w: This is backpressure. An unbounded queue hides overload until the heap is exhausted.

questions.q: Does iterating a `ConcurrentHashMap` while another thread modifies it throw `ConcurrentModificationException`?
o: No: its iterators are weakly consistent
Yes, exactly like a `HashMap`
Yes, but only for removals
Only when the map has more than 1,000 entries
questions.w: Weakly consistent iterators keep going and may or may not reflect later changes. Plain collections use fail-fast iterators.

questions.q: A shared request counter is updated by hundreds of threads. Why might `LongAdder` beat `AtomicLong`?
o: It spreads updates over several cells, so threads retry far less
It uses a global lock that is cheaper
It stores the counter in a database
It guarantees an exact snapshot on every read
questions.w: Under contention many CAS attempts on one variable fail and retry. `LongAdder` sums its cells on read, which is not an atomic snapshot.
